title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #17

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word in this sentence is singular: The seller has an onion and two cabbages? (1 mark)
   A. cabbages
   B. onion
   C. seller has
   D. two

2. What does reading for information mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading the page numbers
   B. Reading only for fun
   C. Reading to learn something new
   D. Reading without understanding

3. Where should letters sit in a lined book? (1 mark)
   A. Outside the margin
   B. Above the page
   C. On the base line
   D. Under the desk

4. Which feeling could a strong, fast voice show? (1 mark)
   A. Sadness
   B. Excitement
   C. Boredom
   D. Sleepiness

5. What does a comma tell a reader? (1 mark)
   A. To shout
   B. To turn the page
   C. To take a short pause
   D. To stop completely

6. Which sentence uses a comma correctly for speaking to someone? (1 mark)
   A. Wanjiku please bring, the umbrella.
   B. Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   C. Wanjiku please bring the, umbrella.
   D. Wanjiku please, bring the umbrella

7. A sentence always begins with (1 mark)
   A. a number
   B. a comma
   C. a capital letter
   D. a full stop

8. Which sentence has the punctuation of a list correct? (1 mark)
   A. We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   B. We wore hats scarves, and coats
   C. We wore hats scarves and coats.
   D. We wore, hats scarves and coats.

9. Which question word asks about a place? (1 mark)
   A. When
   B. Why
   C. Where
   D. Who

10. What is a cue in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. The last words of the person before you
   C. A title
   D. A full stop

11. Where can you check the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. On a clock
   B. In a simple dictionary
   C. In a bag
   D. On a shoe

12. What is a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. A group of animals
   B. A type of word
   C. The order in which things happen
   D. A kind of poem

13. What is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. A saying with no comparison
   B. A comparison using like or as
   C. A long story
   D. A kind of song

14. How can you find the meaning of a new word in a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it always
   B. Tear the page
   C. Ask no one
   D. Use the context and check a dictionary

15. What is a level reader? (1 mark)
   A. A type of dictionary
   B. A book written for a particular reading level
   C. A tool for measuring floors
   D. A machine

16. Why do we explain a proverb in our own words? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To hide it
   C. To change it forever
   D. To show we understand the lesson

17. What is the setting of a story? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the writer
   B. Where and when it happens
   C. The price
   D. The last line

18. What is a portfolio of proverbs? (1 mark)
   A. A poem
   B. A kind of bag for money
   C. A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   D. A game

19. Which is a good way to check a proverb's meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it
   B. Ignore it
   C. Ask an elder or teacher
   D. Guess forever

20. What does a conjunction do? (1 mark)
   A. Describes a colour
   B. Names a thing
   C. Joins words or sentences
   D. Shows a feeling

21. How should you speak when narrating an event? (1 mark)
   A. Angrily always
   B. Without stopping
   C. Clearly and with feeling
   D. Very quietly

22. Which sentence uses when correctly? (1 mark)
   A. When it rained, we ran home.
   B. When we ran home rained it.
   C. We when ran.
   D. Rained we when home.

23. What is a good first step when skimming? (1 mark)
   A. Read every word carefully
   B. Read the title and headings
   C. Skip the page
   D. Close the book

24. What should you check when you reorder jumbled words? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   C. The colour of the letters
   D. The paper

25. What does a simple sentence have? (1 mark)
   A. Two subjects always
   B. No verb
   C. One subject and one predicate
   D. No capital

26. Which tense is used to tell a story about what happened? (1 mark)
   A. The past tense
   B. No tense
   C. Only the future
   D. Only questions

27. What should you do while another speaker is talking in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. Leave
   B. Laugh
   C. Listen without interrupting
   D. Talk loudly

28. What are peers? (1 mark)
   A. People of your own age or class
   B. Only teachers
   C. Only parents
   D. Animals

29. Which interjection shows a request for silence? (1 mark)
   A. Bravo
   B. Shh
   C. Hurray
   D. Aha

30. Which punctuation mark often follows an interjection showing strong feeling? (1 mark)
   A. Full stop
   B. Question mark
   C. Colon
   D. Exclamation mark

31. Which is a mistake in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Using a name
   B. Forgetting the colon after the name
   C. Using a question
   D. Using a full stop

32. A good dialogue should have (1 mark)
   A. no words
   B. an ending
   C. only one word
   D. no characters

33. How should you start a new speaker's words in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Inside a bracket
   B. At the end of the page
   C. On a new line
   D. On the same line as before

34. What should you do if you dialled a wrong number? (1 mark)
   A. Call again angrily
   B. Say sorry and end the call politely
   C. Stay silent
   D. Shout at them

35. What is an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. A word that shows action
   B. A joining word
   C. A word that names a person
   D. A word that describes a noun

36. What is an advertisement? (1 mark)
   A. A weather report
   B. A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   C. A poem
   D. A lesson

37. What is the purpose of the instructions on a form? (1 mark)
   A. To use up space
   B. To make it hard
   C. To tell you how to fill it in
   D. To hide the title

38. What does a good form have? (1 mark)
   A. No title
   B. Tiny words only
   C. No spaces
   D. Clear title, instructions and enough space

39. Which is a good quality of a leader? (1 mark)
   A. Rudeness
   B. Honesty
   C. Cruelty
   D. Laziness

40. Which two words in the poem Lead with honesty rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. fair and strong
   B. poem and song
   C. all and call
   D. leader and rule

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name three parts of a simple form. (3 marks)

42. Divide into subject and predicate: My brother saves coins. (2 marks)

43. List three tips for reciting a poem well. (3 marks)

44. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)

45. A picture shows a girl beside a thin dog under a tree with an empty bowl. Write a story plan and a four-sentence story. (5 marks)

46. What is a vocabulary bank and why is it useful? (2 marks)

47. Explain what the proverb Honesty is the best policy means. (2 marks)

48. Explain how you would perform a choral poem with your class. Include voice, pace and non-verbal cues. (5 marks)

49. Match each interjection with its feeling: (a) Hurray (b) Yuck. (2 marks)

50. Explain the difference in punctuation between Wow! and Oops, it is torn. (3 marks)

51. Explain what to do when you get a small burn and why. (4 marks)

52. Write the plural of each English noun: plate, tomato. (2 marks)

53. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

54. Explain why leaders are important and why people should obey fair leaders. Give two examples of leaders in a community. (5 marks)

55. After listening to a safety story, describe how you would answer four kinds of comprehension questions and give one example of each. (5 marks)

56. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about why we should write neatly. Check your capital letters and full stops. (5 marks)

57. Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans. (3 marks)

58. Read: The nurse bandaged the wound gently and the blood stopped. What does wound mean? Give two clues. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — onion
   Onion names one thing. Cabbages is plural.

2. C — Reading to learn something new
   We read for information to find facts and learn.

3. C — On the base line
   Letters rest on the base line.

4. B — Excitement
   Excitement is often read faster and stronger.

5. C — To take a short pause
   Commas show short pauses.

6. B — Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   A comma follows the name of the person addressed.

7. C — a capital letter
   A capital letter shows the start of a sentence.

8. A — We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   A comma follows each item except the last two, which are joined by and.

9. C — Where
   Where asks for the place.

10. B — The last words of the person before you
   You come in when you hear your cue.

11. B — In a simple dictionary
   Dictionaries give meanings.

12. C — The order in which things happen
   Sequence means order.

13. B — A comparison using like or as
   A simile compares two things using like or as.

14. D — Use the context and check a dictionary
   Context clues and a dictionary help.

15. B — A book written for a particular reading level
   Level readers match the skills of the pupils.

16. D — To show we understand the lesson
   Explaining shows understanding of the meaning.

17. B — Where and when it happens
   Setting means place and time.

18. C — A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   A portfolio holds the class collection.

19. C — Ask an elder or teacher
   Elders can explain the meaning.

20. C — Joins words or sentences
   Conjunctions are joining words.

21. C — Clearly and with feeling
   Clear speech and feeling make a story good.

22. A — When it rained, we ran home.
   It shows two events joined by time.

23. B — Read the title and headings
   The title tells the topic.

24. B — That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   A sentence must make sense.

25. C — One subject and one predicate
   Simple sentences have one main idea.

26. A — The past tense
   Stories about past events use the past.

27. C — Listen without interrupting
   Good debaters listen.

28. A — People of your own age or class
   Peers are people like you in age or class.

29. B — Shh
   Shh asks for quiet.

30. D — Exclamation mark
   Exclamation marks show strong feeling.

31. B — Forgetting the colon after the name
   The colon is needed after the name.

32. B — an ending
   Every piece needs an ending.

33. C — On a new line
   A new line shows a new speaker.

34. B — Say sorry and end the call politely
   Politeness matters.

35. D — A word that describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

36. B — A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   Adverts promote products or services.

37. C — To tell you how to fill it in
   Instructions guide the person filling it.

38. D — Clear title, instructions and enough space
   Clarity makes forms easy to fill.

39. B — Honesty
   Good leaders are honest and fair.

40. C — all and call
   All and call have the same ending sound.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, instructions, fields, signature, date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Subject: My brother. Predicate: saves coins.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Learn it well, mark pauses and stressed words, speak clearly, look at the audience, keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan with title, characters, setting, problem and ending, followed by four sentences that show the girl helping the dog and end with a lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, setting and problem, and two marks for a clear four-sentence story.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a class list of words on one theme. It helps pupils remember and use new words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the use.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Telling the truth is always the wisest choice because it builds trust.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the reason.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Learn the poem well, keep the same pace together, speak clearly with expression, use gestures and smiles as non-verbal cues, look at the audience and practise beforehand.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of five points.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) joy (b) disgust
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma after a mild interjection shows a softer feeling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each punctuation mark and one for the difference.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water for several minutes to reduce pain, cover it with a clean cloth and tell an adult or go to a clinic.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for cool water, the reason, clean cover and telling an adult.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: plates, tomatoes
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Leaders guide, make decisions and keep order. Obeying fair leaders keeps peace and safety. Examples: chief, teacher, class monitor, elders.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for why leaders are important, two marks for obeying and one for examples.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: Answer who with a person (his mother), what with an event (touched the pot), where with a place (the clinic) and why with a reason (he wanted to see the steam). Give short, full answers and ask for repetition if needed.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each kind and example, and one mark for full sentences.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three neat, complete sentences, for example Neat writing helps others to read my work. It shows respect for the reader. I feel proud when my book is tidy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence, one mark for capital letters and one for full stops.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
   Working / marking points: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wound is an injury. Clues are the nurse, bandaged and blood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and two marks for clues, awarding one for each up to two.
